  ```
  WITH first_order AS (
    SELECT customer_id, DATE_TRUNC('month', MIN(order_date)) AS first_month
    FROM iceberg.analytics.orders
    GROUP BY customer_id
  ),
  new_per_month AS (
    SELECT first_month AS order_month, COUNT(*) AS new_customers
    FROM first_order GROUP BY first_month
  )
  SELECT order_month, new_customers,
    SUM(new_customers) OVER (ORDER BY order_month
      ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS cumulative_distinct_customers
  FROM new_per_month ORDER BY order_month;
  ```

=== DOCS-TRUTH VERIFIED (trino.io/docs/467 via WebFetch on 2026-06-08) ===
• MIN(order_date) GROUP BY customer_id — VALID: Trino aggregate-page confirms 'min() Returns the minimum value of all input values' for any comparable type including DATE/TIMESTAMP. Each-customer's-first-period via MIN+GROUP BY is the standard idiom.
• SUM(x) OVER (ORDER BY col ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) — VALID: documented as running-sum form across Trino 467 window docs; already canonicalized in this file at Pattern A r07:1700+ and Pattern A2 r07:1868+ with same ROWS frame.
• COUNT(DISTINCT col) OVER (...) — NOT supported in Trino 467 (trinodb/trino #7885 still open). Documented as banned form at r07:638-740 (PRIMARY HLL workaround, SECONDARY exact-self-join workaround) and now ALSO at the new r07:2117 DO-NOT-WRITE row (c). Pattern A4 sidesteps this limitation by precomputing first-appearance counts (plain GROUP BY aggregate, no DISTINCT inside window) then running-SUM-ing those (plain window-SUM, no DISTINCT inside window).
• cumulative-distinct ≡ running-SUM-of-first-appearances identity — mathematically correct: each entity contributes +1 exactly once (in their first-appearance period only), so the running-SUM of first-appearance counts through period N equals exactly the cardinality of the set of entities whose first appearance was on or before period N = cumulative distinct entities ever through period N. The identity holds for any grain (day/week/month) and any first-appearance criterion (first order, first paid, first event, first signup).
